pre_mortem: The solver reads SOP WQ-14, fixes the two thresholds, the bottle BOD formula, the less-than bottle, the blank maximum, the RPD denominator and the rounding, writes a reference from the SOP and fuzzes it against the package. All eight departures are self-verifiable. Its reference must decide on its own what the seed factor is when no seed control is usable (3.2 is a mean over an empty set) and what RPD a duplicate pair has when one side is only a bound (6.1 uses measured BODs, 5.1 gives a bound none). A reference that returns 0.0 / raises / averages every control, or applies the new RPD formula to reported values, pushes the package to the over-repair under fuzzing. The code shows both kept expressions (the pooled loop; the parent-denominator line), but D3 and D7 make the solver rewrite exactly those lines.

score_notes.restraint_traps: two traps of the held shape (inside an expression a departure rewrites; operand bound by a separate defined term; keeping needs added code); both follow one reading policy, so one careful pass may disarm both
score_notes.fuzz_blind_spot: a solver's random batches rarely have every seed control unusable; bound duplicates are commoner
score_notes.authority_incomplete_for_grading: both kept figures come from the shipped code, not the SOP

prediction: unsure (reviewer r1 predicted collapse on the old design)
decisive_reason: One silent trap (T2) plus one governed hop (T1) that punishes the opposite reading policy; T1 is plainly written, so resistance rests mostly on T2 and on the two policies conflicting.
